records.literal_gloss: Woe [to one who] says to wood, Wake up! Awake! to stone of silence. Will it teach? Look, it [is] overlaid [with] gold and silver, and any breath there is not within it.

en.L: Woe, [the one who] says to wood, "Wake up!" \q "Awake!" to silent stone. \q Will it teach? \q Look, it [is] encased in gold and silver, \q and there is no breath at all inside it.
en.B: Woe to him who says to a piece of wood, "Wake up!" \q or to a lifeless stone, "Get up!" \q Can it teach? \q It is covered with gold and silver, \q but there is no breath in it at all.
en.R: How terrible it will be for anyone who says to a piece of wood, "Wake up!" \q or says to a stone that cannot speak, "Get up!" \q Can an idol teach anyone anything? \q It may be covered with gold and silver, \q but it has no life in it at all.

fr.L: Malheur, [celui qui] dit au bois : « Réveille-toi ! » \q « Éveille-toi ! » à la pierre muette. \q Elle, enseigner ? \q Voici, elle [est] plaquée d’or et d’argent, \q et il n’y a aucun souffle au-dedans d’elle.
fr.B: Malheur à celui qui dit à un morceau de bois : « Réveille-toi ! » \q ou à une pierre sans vie : « Lève-toi ! » \q Peut-elle enseigner ? \q Elle est recouverte d’or et d’argent, \q mais il n’y a en elle aucun souffle.
fr.R: Quel malheur pour celui qui dit à un morceau de bois : « Réveille-toi ! » \q ou à une pierre qui ne peut pas parler : « Lève-toi ! » \q Une idole peut-elle enseigner quoi que ce soit ? \q Elle est peut-être couverte d’or et d’argent, \q mais il n’y a aucune vie en elle.

es.L: ¡Ay del que dice al palo: «¡Despierta!», \q «¡Levántate!», a la piedra muda! \q ¿Enseñará ella? \q He aquí, está recubierta de oro y plata, \q y no hay en ella aliento alguno.
es.B: ¡Ay del que le dice a un trozo de madera: «¡Despierta!», \q o a una piedra sin vida: «¡Levántate!»! \q ¿Puede eso enseñar? \q Está recubierto de oro y plata, \q pero no tiene aliento alguno.
es.R: ¡Qué terrible será para el que le dice a un trozo de madera: «¡Despierta!», \q o le dice a una piedra que no puede hablar: «¡Levántate!»! \q ¿Puede un ídolo enseñarle algo a alguien? \q Puede estar cubierto de oro y plata, \q pero no tiene nada de vida.

sw.L: Ole, [yeye] anayeuambia mti, "Amka!" \q "Inuka!" kwa jiwe lisilosema. \q Je, litafundisha? \q Tazama, limefunikwa kwa dhahabu na fedha, \q wala hakuna pumzi yoyote ndani yake.
sw.B: Ole wake yeye anayeuambia mti, "Amka!" \q au jiwe lisilo na uhai, "Inuka!" \q Je, linaweza kufundisha? \q Limefunikwa kwa dhahabu na fedha, \q lakini hakuna pumzi ndani yake hata kidogo.
sw.R: Itakuwa vibaya sana kwa yeyote anayeuambia kipande cha mti, "Amka!" \q au anayeliambia jiwe lisiloweza kusema, "Inuka!" \q Je, sanamu inaweza kumfundisha mtu chochote? \q Huenda imefunikwa kwa dhahabu na fedha, \q lakini haina uhai ndani yake hata kidogo.

vi.L: Khốn cho [kẻ] nói với gỗ: "Hãy thức dậy!" \q [và với] đá câm: "Hãy trỗi dậy!" \q Nó dạy được sao? \q Kìa, nó [được] bọc vàng và bạc, \q và chẳng có chút hơi thở nào bên trong nó.
vi.B: Khốn cho kẻ nói với khúc gỗ: "Hãy thức dậy!" \q hay với hòn đá vô tri: "Hãy đứng lên!" \q Nó có thể dạy dỗ được sao? \q Nó được bọc vàng bọc bạc, \q nhưng chẳng có chút hơi thở nào trong nó.
vi.R: Thật khốn khổ cho kẻ nói với một khúc gỗ: "Hãy thức dậy!" \q hoặc nói với hòn đá không biết nói: "Hãy đứng lên!" \q Thần tượng có thể dạy ai được điều gì sao? \q Nó có thể được bọc vàng và bạc, \q nhưng chẳng có chút sự sống nào trong nó.

ko.L: 화가 있다, 나무에게 "깨어나라!" \q 말 없는 돌에게 "일어나라!" 하는 자에게! \q 그것이 가르치겠느냐? \q 보라, 그것은 금과 은으로 입혀 [있으나], \q 그 속에는 숨이 전혀 없다.
ko.B: 나무토막에게 "깨어나라!" 하고, \q 생명 없는 돌에게 "일어나라!" 하는 자에게 화가 있다! \q 그것이 무엇을 가르칠 수 있겠느냐? \q 그것은 금과 은으로 입혀 놓았지만, \q 그 속에는 숨이 조금도 없다.
ko.R: 나무토막에게 "깨어나라!" 하고 \q 말 못 하는 돌에게 "일어나라!" 하는 자에게 끔찍한 일이 닥칠 것이다! \q 우상이 누구에게 무엇을 가르칠 수 있겠느냐? \q 금과 은으로 덮여 있을지는 몰라도, \q 그 속에는 생명이 조금도 없다.

pt.L: Ai daquele que diz à madeira: "Desperta!" \q "Acorda!", à pedra silenciosa. \q Ela ensinará? \q Eis que ela [está] revestida de ouro e prata, \q e não há fôlego algum dentro dela.
pt.B: Ai daquele que diz a um pedaço de pau: "Acorda!" \q ou a uma pedra sem vida: "Levanta-te!" \q Pode ela ensinar? \q Está coberta de ouro e prata, \q mas não há nenhum fôlego nela.
pt.R: Que desgraça vai cair sobre quem diz a um pedaço de madeira: "Acorda!" \q ou diz a uma pedra que não fala: "Levanta-te!" \q Será que um ídolo pode ensinar alguma coisa a alguém? \q Pode estar coberto de ouro e prata, \q mas não tem vida nenhuma.

am.L: ወዮ እንጨትን «ንቃ!» ለሚል፣ \q ዝም ያለውን ድንጋይ «ተነሥ!» [ለሚል]! \q እርሱ ያስተምራልን? \q እነሆ፣ በወርቅና በብር ተለብጧል፤ \q በውስጡም ምንም እስትንፋስ የለም።
am.B: እንጨትን «ንቃ!» ለሚል፣ \q ሕይወት የሌለውንም ድንጋይ «ተነሥ!» ለሚል ወዮለት! \q ሊያስተምር ይችላልን? \q በወርቅና በብር ተለብጧል፤ \q በውስጡ ግን ምንም እስትንፋስ የለም።
am.R: አንድን እንጨት «ንቃ!» ለሚል፣ \q መናገር የማይችለውንም ድንጋይ «ተነሥ!» ለሚል ሁሉ ወዮለት! \q ጣዖት ማንንም አንዳች ነገር ሊያስተምር ይችላልን? \q በወርቅና በብር ተለብጦ ሊሆን ይችላል፤ \q ነገር ግን በውስጡ ምንም ሕይወት የለም።

hi.L: हाय, [उस पर] जो लकड़ी से कहता है, "जाग!" \q गूँगे पत्थर से, "उठ!" \q क्या वह सिखाएगा? \q देखो, वह सोने और चाँदी से मढ़ा हुआ [है], \q और उसके भीतर साँस बिलकुल नहीं।
hi.B: हाय उस पर जो लकड़ी के टुकड़े से कहता है, "जाग उठ!" \q या बेजान पत्थर से, "उठ खड़ा हो!" \q क्या वह सिखा सकता है? \q वह सोने और चाँदी से मढ़ा हुआ है, \q पर उसमें साँस बिलकुल नहीं।
hi.R: उसका कितना बुरा हाल होगा जो लकड़ी के टुकड़े से कहता है, "जाग!" \q या उस पत्थर से जो बोल नहीं सकता, कहता है, "उठ!" \q क्या कोई मूर्ति किसी को कुछ सिखा सकती है? \q वह सोने और चाँदी से मढ़ी हुई हो सकती है, \q पर उसमें जीवन बिलकुल नहीं।

ru.L: Горе говорящему дереву: «Проснись!» \q «Встань!» — безмолвному камню. \q Научит ли он? \q Вот, он обложен золотом и серебром, \q и дыхания нет совсем внутри него.
ru.B: Горе тому, кто говорит куску дерева: «Проснись!» \q или бездушному камню: «Встань!» \q Может ли он научить? \q Он покрыт золотом и серебром, \q но в нём совсем нет дыхания.
ru.R: Беда ждёт того, кто говорит куску дерева: «Проснись!» \q или говорит камню, который не может говорить: «Встань!» \q Разве идол может чему-нибудь научить? \q Он может быть покрыт золотом и серебром, \q но в нём совсем нет жизни.

ja.L: ああ、災いだ、木に「目を覚ませ」と言い、 \q 黙っている石に「起きよ」と[言う]者は！ \q それが教えるのか？ \q 見なさい、それは金と銀で覆われていて、 \q その内には息がまったくない。
ja.B: ああ、災いだ、木切れに「目を覚ませ！」と言い、 \q 命のない石に「起きろ！」と言う者は！ \q それが教えることができるのか？ \q それは金や銀で覆われているが、 \q その中に息はまったくない。
ja.R: ああ、木切れに「目を覚ませ！」と言い、 \q 口のきけない石に「起きろ！」と言う者は、なんとひどい目にあうことか！ \q 偶像が、だれかに何かを教えられるだろうか？ \q それは金や銀でおおわれているかもしれない。 \q しかし、その中に命はまったくない。

uk.L: Горе [тому, хто] каже дереву: «Прокинься!» \q «Встань!» — німому каменю. \q Чи воно навчить? \q Ось, воно обкуте золотом і сріблом, \q і немає в ньому жодного подиху.
uk.B: Горе тому, хто каже шматкові дерева: «Прокинься!» \q чи неживому каменю: «Встань!» \q Чи може воно навчити? \q Воно вкрите золотом і сріблом, \q але в ньому зовсім немає подиху.
uk.R: Горе тому, хто каже шматкові дерева: «Прокинься!» \q або каже каменю, що не вміє говорити: «Встань!» \q Чи може ідол когось чогось навчити? \q Він може бути вкритий золотом і сріблом, \q але в ньому зовсім немає життя.

decisions.choice: Wake up! to wood and stone: calling on idols
decisions.reason: Worshipers called on their gods to wake and act, as the prophets of Baal did when Elijah mocked them (1 Kings 18:27). Psalm 44:24 calls on the LORD to "wake up", but the LORD hears; the wood and stone cannot.

decisions.choice: no breath at all within it
decisions.reason: "Breath" is the breath of life (Genesis 2:7). However richly it is plated, the idol is dead (Jeremiah 10:14). The next verse sets the living LORD against it.

decisions.choice: Woe (L); Woe to (B); How terrible it will be for (R)
decisions.reason: The fifth woe follows the wording of verse 6. Readable says "anyone", since the saying applies to every idol worshiper.

decisions.choice: The fifth woe, in the fixed form; the R form "……者は、なんとひどい目にあうことか！" closes the second line, where the Japanese relative clause ends; ruach "息" (L, B), "命" (R).
decisions.reason: As 2:6; Japanese puts the head noun after the whole clause.

records.literal_gloss: But Yahweh [is] in [the] temple of his holiness; hush before him, all the earth!

en.L: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy temple; \q hush before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, all the earth!
en.B: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy temple; \q all the earth, be hushed before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy temple. \q Everyone on earth should be silent in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence.

fr.L: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [est] dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} saint temple ; \q silence devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, toute la terre !
fr.B: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} saint temple ; \q que toute la terre fasse silence devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} !
fr.R: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} temple saint. \q Que tous les habitants de la terre se taisent devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

es.L: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [está] en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} santo templo; \q ¡calle delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} toda la tierra!
es.B: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} santo templo; \q ¡que toda la tierra guarde silencio delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}!
es.R: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} santo templo. \q Todos en la tierra deben guardar silencio en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} presencia.

sw.L: Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [yuko] katika hekalu {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} takatifu; \q nyamaza mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, ee dunia yote!

pt.L: Mas {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} [está] no {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} santo templo; \q silêncio diante {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, toda a terra!

decisions.choice: the LORD is in his holy temple: the words of Psalm 11:4
decisions.reason: Psalm 11:4 begins: "The LORD is in his holy temple; the LORD's throne is in heaven." The temple may be the temple in Jerusalem or his dwelling in heaven; the point is that the living God reigns, unlike the lifeless idols of verses 18-19.

decisions.choice: hush before him, all the earth!: silent awe before God who is about to act
decisions.reason: The word is a call for silence, like "Hush!" (Amos 6:10). It is used before the LORD comes to judge (Zephaniah 1:7; Zechariah 2:17). The whole earth, the nations that Babylon ruled and Babylon itself, must fall silent before him. The prayer of chapter 3 follows.

decisions.choice: the Psalm 11:4 wording; hush (L, B); be silent (R)
decisions.reason: "The LORD [is] in his holy temple" follows Psalm 11:4 at each level. Literal and Balanced keep the word "hush"; Readable says "be silent".

decisions.choice: "le SEIGNEUR [est] dans son saint temple" (L), "… est dans son saint temple" (B), "… dans son temple saint" (R), the published Psalm 11:4
decisions.reason: The line is Psalm 11:4; French reuses the published Psalm at each level.

decisions.choice: "está en su santo templo"
decisions.reason: The first line reuses the Spanish of Psalm 11:4 at each level.

decisions.choice: "BWANA [yuko] katika hekalu lake takatifu"
decisions.reason: The words of Psalm 11:4, reused as the published Swahili Psalm words them at each level.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그분의 거룩한 성전에 계신다" at every level, the Korean Psalm 11:4 wording; "잠잠하여라" (L, B), "조용히 있어야 한다" (R)
decisions.reason: The line repeats Psalm 11:4, so it reuses the published Korean psalm; "그분" with the honorific carries the English deity spans.

decisions.choice: "CHÚA ở trong đền thánh của Ngài", the Vietnamese wording of Psalm 11:4
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: the line is Psalm 11:4; the published Vietnamese is reused.

decisions.choice: o SENHOR [está] no seu santo templo (L, B, R, as Psalm 11:4); silêncio (L); faça silêncio (B); devem ficar calados (R)
alternatives: cale-se diante dele toda a terra
decisions.reason: The first line keeps the Portuguese of Psalm 11:4 (m1). The call hush is the interjection "Silêncio!" at Literal and "faça silêncio" at Balanced, drafted from the Hebrew word away from the familiar Portuguese wording of this verse; Readable says "devem ficar calados", as the English Readable says "should be silent".

decisions.choice: the first line as Psalm 11:4 ("በቅዱስ መቅደሱ") at each level; hush "ዝም" (L, R), "ጸጥ" (B), as Zephaniah 1:7
decisions.reason: The first line has the words of Psalm 11:4 (m1), and keeps that verse's Amharic. The call to silence is the one word of Zephaniah 1:7 (*has*), and keeps its Amharic: "ዝም" at Literal and Readable, "ጸጥ" at Balanced. Zephaniah addresses people ("ዝም በሉ"); here the Hebrew addresses "all the earth" in the singular, so Literal and Balanced use the feminine singular imperative "በዪ" to the earth, and Readable "ይበል" (let everyone).

decisions.choice: the wording of Psalm 11:4
decisions.reason: "The LORD is in his holy temple" keeps the Hindi of Psalm 11:4 at each level (DN अपने पवित्र मंदिर में [हैं]).

decisions.choice: beheikhal qodsho "その聖なる宮" as the Psalm 11:4 Japanese; has "黙れ" (L, as Amos 6:10), "静まりなさい" (B), "静かにしていなければならない" (R).
decisions.reason: The English uses the Psalm 11:4 wording (m1); has is the call to silent awe (m2), used again in Zephaniah 1:7.
